alternatives.root_cause: product-catalog shipped a broken artifact that fails GetProduct
alternatives.why_not: The change log for product-catalog is empty over 24h (tr_0d60a32b7898), so no artifact reference changed; and the service still serves successful requests with healthy store queries in the same window.

alternatives.root_cause: frontend-proxy or frontend is itself generating the errors it alerted on
alternatives.why_not: Both carry the identical downstream error payload and their spans end at the same instant as the product-catalog child span (tr_03374cd34f6a), which is propagation, not origination; frontend's change log is also empty (tr_a304d1b70a3a).

alternatives.root_cause: product-reviews became slow and dragged the frontend past its deadlines
alternatives.why_not: Its spans are the slowest hop in some traces but complete in tens of milliseconds without errors, which does not produce the gRPC INTERNAL failures seen at the frontend.

verdict.summary: A runtime feature flag on product-catalog makes its GetProduct handler fail, and those gRPC errors propagate up through frontend to frontend-proxy, which alerted.
verdict.reasoning: Traces from the alerting edge show the error originating at the product-catalog GetProduct span and being re-raised unchanged by frontend and frontend-proxy, so the callers are reporting a failure they did not cause (tr_03374cd34f6a). product-catalog's change log is empty over a 24h window (tr_0d60a32b7898) and frontend's is empty too (tr_a304d1b70a3a), so no artifact or config file changed; a flag flipped in the flag store is the only mechanism that produces failures with an empty change log. frontend's own logs carry an upstream gRPC INTERNAL from product-catalog continuously through the end of the window (tr_c949fa9e8a7d). product-catalog spans that do not hit the flagged path still complete in under a few ms with healthy store queries, which rules out exhaustion, slow dependency, freeze, partition and disk pressure.
open_questions: The error-ratio series for product-catalog, frontend and frontend-proxy showed no sustained departure from baseline in the queried window (tr_d3fb89d9a781, tr_df120b974d84, tr_b50744114147), so the metric evidence does not corroborate the 15:54:16 onset and the failure may have been present well before the alert fired.
Failing calls appear as far back as the start of the observed window, so the actual flip time is not established and may precede the stated onset.
A direct log query against product-catalog returned empty on retry (tr_79fe8eeb21b2), so the service's own account of the failure was not independently confirmed.
Whether the other blast-radius services (cart, checkout, ad, recommendation, product-reviews) were affected by the same cause or only by shared frontend pages was not examined.
